free_tier.stated: A free first LoRA fine-tune with no card: 'Muse Glimmer 30B SFT is free via UI and Serverless Training API until 11/30. No credit card required.' The promotion applies to LoRA SFT jobs started before 2026-12-01T00:00:00-08:00 and covers training only: 'RL, DPO, full-parameter training, deployments, and inference outside the training run are not covered.' In-session evaluation sampling is billed at the published per-token rates.

retention.stated: the 2026-11-30 window binds, not a quota: there is no published cap on the number of free LoRA SFT jobs inside the window, and the day the window closes the same job is refused unless it is run with --allow-paid.

interface_detail: HTTPS REST: the Serverless Training API endpoint is https://api.fireworks.ai/training/v1/serverless, reached through the Python SDK; documented, not probed
tooling: the provider documents the Python SDK (pip install "fireworks-ai[training]"), the firectl CLI, the fw-ai/cookbook training examples and the dashboard UI
chaining: it composes with hosted inference lanes: train the LoRA adapter here inside the promotion window, download it with firectl model download, and serve it on a hosted lane that accepts a LoRA adapter on the same base. On Fireworks itself a trained LoRA can only be deployed to an on-demand (dedicated) deployment, which the promotion does not cover; serverless deployment of LoRA models is not supported. The adapter needs the exact base it was trained on, and whether the Muse Glimmer base weights can also be downloaded is not stated (unverified).

limits.value: the 2026-11-30 window binds, not a quota: there is no published cap on the number of free LoRA SFT jobs inside the window, and the day the window closes the same job is refused unless it is run with --allow-paid.

10 requests per minute account-wide while the account has no payment method or no credits; with a payment method and active credits the ceiling is 6,000 requests per minute. The cap is one envelope shared by every model and every API, not a per-model request limit; requests above it are rejected (for example HTTP 429).

serverless limits per model are tokens per minute, not requests: three adaptive meters (total prompt, uncached prompt and generated TPM) start at an unpublished default and rise 25% at most once every 15 minutes toward a ceiling set by model size and spend tier. The published ceilings (for a model under 800B parameters: 216M total prompt, 54M uncached prompt and 2.16M generated TPM) apply at Tier 3 and above; the ceiling of an account with no payment method is not published.

concurrency, not a rate: the Serverless Training API allows 8 active runs per account by default (account overrides may differ); some pool models also cap active runs per account on that base model, with managed fine-tuning jobs on it counting toward the cap, and a run over either cap fails with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

reliability_note: an account that finishes its $1 credit with no payment method is suspended until a payment method is added; with credits exhausted and Auto Reload off, usage pauses until credits are added.

notes: What is free here is the training loop, not tokens. Serverless inference carries no advertised signup credit: the pricing page reads 'Simply add a payment method to buy credits, and usage is then deducted from your balance.' Whether a new account still holds a starting balance is unverified: behind a sign-up. The promotion names one base model and excludes RL, DPO, full-parameter training, deployments and inference outside the training run, so it is not a general free-training lane. No cap on the number of free jobs is published; the concurrency cap is in limits.
